title: Explicit three-dimensional tensors of superlinear rank
formal: Do there exist one deterministic multitape Turing machine \(A\), a real constant \(K>0\) and an integer \(a\ge1\) such that, for every \(n\ge1\), on input \(1^n\) it outputs all entries of a rational tensor \(T_n\in\mathbb Q^{n\times n\times n}\) within \(K(n+1)^a\) bit operations, and \[\forall B\in\mathbb R_{>0}\ \exists N\ge1\ \forall n\ge N:\quad \operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}(T_n)\ge Bn?\] Here rank is ordinary tensor rank over the complex numbers. Thus the required ratio \(\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb C}(T_n)/n\) tends to infinity, with no prescribed rate.
why: Tensor rank measures the number of independent bilinear products needed to express a computation. Explicit superlinear-rank families would turn generic hardness into concrete examples and yield lower bounds for the corresponding constant-degree arithmetic computations.

importance.reason: A central explicit lower-bound challenge for tensor rank and arithmetic computation: the gap between generic quadratic rank and explicit linear lower bounds persists even for three-way tensors and relates directly to unrestricted arithmetic circuit barriers.

sentences: A three-way tensor is a cubic array, and its ordinary rank is the fewest rank-one arrays whose sum equals it.
The selected branch asks for rational entries written by one deterministic algorithm in polynomial time in the dimension.
Rank is measured over the complex numbers, and its ratio to the side length must tend to infinity.
The algorithm must produce every dimension without advice, symbolic number-field entries or uncharged output bits.
Known explicit linear border-rank bounds and recent semi-explicit high-rank constructions do not meet this superlinear rational-output target.

definitions:
A tensor \(T\in\mathbb Q^{n\times n\times n}\) is the array \((T_{ijk})_{1\le i,j,k\le n}\), regarded as an element of \(\mathbb C^n\otimes\mathbb C^n\otimes\mathbb C^n\) through the usual inclusion of the rationals into the complex numbers. Its ordinary rank is the smallest integer \(r\ge0\) for which there are vectors \(u^{(s)},v^{(s)},w^{(s)}\in\mathbb C^n\), for \(1\le s\le r\), satisfying
\[
T_{ijk}=\sum_{s=1}^{r}u^{(s)}_i\,v^{(s)}_j\,w^{(s)}_k
\quad\text{for every }1\le i,j,k\le n.
\]
An empty sum is the zero tensor. The factors in a rank decomposition may be arbitrary complex vectors, although the constructed tensor entries are rational. No symmetry is required. The target is not matrix rank of an array rearrangement, slice rank, border rank, or an asymptotic tensor-power rank.

The machine outputs the \(n^3\) entries in lexicographic order of \((i,j,k)\). Each entry is an explicitly written signed binary integer numerator and positive binary integer denominator, with delimiters. All bits are charged, so their total length and each individual entry's bit length are polynomially bounded in \(n\). A symbolic power, root-of-unity description, unevaluated arithmetic expression or arbitrary real constant is not a rational-entry output under this convention. All input reading, integer arithmetic, preprocessing and output writing count. The finite program and \(K,a\) are independent of \(n\); there is no advice, oracle, randomness or uncharged preprocessing.

The algorithm is required on every positive integer dimension, and the rank guarantee holds for all sufficiently large dimensions for each \(B\). The integer threshold \(N\) may depend on \(B\) and the fixed family; it is not required to be computed. No rank decomposition, rank value or lower-bound certificate is an output requirement for \(A\); the rank-growth guarantee must instead be established by the submitted proof. Explicitness here means polynomial time in the dimension to write the whole tensor, not a separate polylogarithmic-time entry-query requirement.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of the existence of such a finite construction algorithm, its uniform polynomial bit-cost bound and the entire eventual superlinear rank guarantee, or a complete Lean proof that no such algorithm exists. An existence proof without the construction cost, a fixed constant multiple of the dimension, growth only along an unspecified subsequence, or a conditional lower bound alone does not meet this target. Any growth rate tending to infinity in the displayed normalized rank suffices; a fixed positive power improvement is not required.

context_blocks.text: Open Problem 15 asks for explicit three-dimensional tensors of superlinear rank after explaining their connection to arithmetic circuits. The survey writes the ground field generically and leaves representation details implicit. This card selects the characteristic-zero branch with rationally encoded entries and rank over the complex numbers; it does not claim equivalence to every possible field or algebraic-number encoding.

The full-output polynomial-time convention follows the explicitness discussion in Definition 1.1 of Landsberg and Michałek. Their construction uses integer coordinates, and their border-rank lower bound grows linearly with the dimension. Such a result is meaningful progress but does not make the rank-to-dimension ratio tend to infinity.

The July 2026 sumset-expansion paper explicitly distinguishes efficiently constructible tensor entries from short algebraic descriptions. Its high-border-rank tensors use number-field coordinates and are described as semi-explicit; they do not constitute the rational bit-output construction fixed here. Its Remark 5 still states the explicit superlinear-rank challenge.

The target asks for ordinary rank. A superlinear lower bound on border rank would be sufficient, but proving that stronger property is not required. Conversely, improved linear bounds for either notion do not settle the superlinear target.

checked_sources: Read Shpilka–Yehudayoff Section 3.8.2, Theorem 3.23 and Open Problem 15. The target is ordinary rank omega(n) for order three, not the subsequent growing-order tensor/formula problem.

Read Landsberg–Michalek Theory of Computing 21(13), Introduction, Definition 1.1, Theorem 1.2 and Section 3 Lemmas 3.1–3.2. Its explicitness is polynomial in the dimension, with integer-coordinate constructions. The 2.02n border-rank result is linear and cannot settle omega(n). The PDF and landing page differ by one day on the December 2025 publication date; the card uses only the year.

Read Narayanan arXiv:2607.15848v1 Section 1.6, Theorem 5, Section 5.2 and Remark 5. It explicitly labels the high-rank root-of-unity tensors semi-explicit and still states that explicit three-way superlinear-rank tensors are not known. Short root-of-unity descriptions do not satisfy rational bit-output requirements.

Documented the fixed characteristic-zero branch because the original survey uses an unspecified ground field. Polynomial full-output construction follows the later precise explicitness convention; no stronger polylogarithmic entry algorithm or fixed power rank gain was imposed.

Bounded subsequent searches through 2026-09-16 found conditional fine-grained tensor lower bounds and the July semi-explicit construction, not a matching unconditional rational-output family. The cited linear and semi-explicit proofs were not independently certified in full.
